headline: Cybercriminals pivot to healthcare's softer vendor targets as fresh breaches strike DHS and Dutch carrier Odido, and the NSA rebuilds its elite offensive-hacking unit.

emerging_trends.text: Cybercriminals are shifting from hospitals to their suppliers, with attacks on healthcare service providers more than doubling in the first half of 2026 because the softer supply-chain targets prove easier to breach.
The privacy tools people trust are leaking their data, as researchers found 281 free Android VPN apps installed more than 2.4 billion times spilling traffic and tracking users.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Free Android VPN Apps Leak User Traffic

emerging_trends.text: Governments are sharpening their offensive posture, with the NSA reviving its Tailored Access Operations hacking unit even as a Department of Homeland Security database falls to intruders.
emerging_trends.topic_title: NSA Revives TAO as DHS Database Falls

topics.title: Healthcare Service Providers Under Siege
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reported July 10, 2026 that cyberattacks on healthcare service providers and other healthcare businesses more than doubled in the first half of 2026, even as attacks on hospitals and clinics grew only modestly.
topics.summary: Attackers increasingly target the vendors, billing firms, and support businesses surrounding hospitals rather than the hospitals themselves, since these providers hold patient data and often run weaker defenses; healthcare organizations should extend monitoring and vendor-risk reviews to their third parties.

sources.title: Cybercriminals Flock to Healthcare Businesses as Attacks Surge

topics.title: Jailed Launderer Steals Seized Crypto
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer reported July 10, 2026 that a Bulgarian national serving a 121-month sentence for laundering millions stolen from American fraud victims now faces charges of stealing $290,000 in government-seized cryptocurrency from behind bars.
topics.summary: The case shows seized digital assets stay reachable even after conviction and imprisonment, deepening an existing money-laundering prosecution tied to US fraud proceeds.

sources.title: Money launderer accused of stealing seized crypto while in prison

topics.title: NSA Revives TAO as DHS Database Falls
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported July 10, 2026 that the National Security Agency is reviving its Tailored Access Operations offensive-hacking unit, that intruders hacked a Department of Homeland Security database, and that Canadian authorities disrupted ransomware operations, while Adobe boosted its patch cadence and Anthropic sued Abnormal AI.
topics.summary: The developments signal a more aggressive US government cyber stance alongside a fresh federal data exposure; agencies and contractors should watch for follow-on disclosures on the DHS breach.

sources.title: In Other News: DHS Database Hacked, Adobe Boosts Patch Cadence, Canada Disrupts Ransomware Ops

topics.title: Free Android VPN Apps Leak User Traffic
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News reported July 10, 2026 that researchers ran 281 of the most popular free VPN apps on the Google Play Store through a new testing system and found many fail at basic privacy, with 29 apps leaking user traffic outside the tunnel across apps installed more than 2.4 billion times.
topics.summary: Free Android VPN apps marketed for privacy expose the very data they promise to protect through traffic leaks, unencrypted transmission, and tracking; users and employers should treat free mobile VPNs as untrusted and move to vetted paid services.

sources.title: Study of 281 Free Android VPN Apps Finds Traffic Leaks, Unencrypted Data, and Tracking

topics.title: ATM and BitLocker Cryptographic Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading detailed July 10, 2026 fresh bugs in a Microsoft BitLocker security wrapper that put organizations, and possibly ATMs, at risk of compromise.
topics.summary: Holes in software that wraps Microsoft BitLocker disk encryption could let attackers undermine protected systems including cash machines; affected operators should track the vendor fix and audit BitLocker-dependent deployments.

sources.title: Fresh ATM Crypto Software Bugs: Jackpot or Bust?

topics.title: Dutch Hackers Tied to Odido Telecom Breach
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer reported July 10, 2026 that the Dutch National Police found strong indications that Dutch hackers carried out the February 2026 breach of telecommunications provider Odido.
topics.summary: Odido, one of the Netherlands' largest mobile carriers, suffered a February intrusion that police now attribute to domestic hackers; customers should stay alert to phishing that abuses any exposed contact data.

sources.title: Police suspects Dutch hackers were involved in Odido breach

business_politics.title: Iran Strikes Gulf Arab States as Hormuz Fight Widens
business_politics.latest_developments: Iran fired on targets in Jordan, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Qatar, turning weeks of threats against its Gulf Arab neighbors into actual strikes as U.S. Central Command hit Iranian targets again.
business_politics.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard attacked a containership transiting the Strait of Hormuz, again declared the waterway closed, and drew fresh United States strikes, and Tehran has now retaliated across five Gulf Arab states, menacing the tenuous ceasefire and the world's most important oil chokepoint.

sources.title: US launches fresh strikes after Tehran declares Strait of Hormuz closed
U.S. and Iran Launch New Attacks in Fight to Control the Strait of Hormuz

business.title: Housing Act Becomes Law With Pittsburgh Roots
business.latest_developments: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act automatically became law at 12 a.m. Saturday, July 12, after President Trump declined to sign it to protest Senate inaction on the SAVE America Act.
business.summary: The bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, the most comprehensive federal housing legislation in decades and shaped in part by Pittsburgh-area advocates, aims to expand housing supply, lower costs, and curb institutional investors from buying up homes.

sources.title: Sweeping housing bill with roots in Pittsburgh area has now become law — without Trump's signature
Bipartisan housing bill automatically becomes law after Trump refuses to sign it

around_town.title: Dangerous Heat Wave Builds Over Western Pennsylvania
around_town.latest_developments: Forecasters expect temperatures to climb back into the 90s across the Pittsburgh region this week as an oppressive heat wave spreads over much of the United States.
around_town.summary: Days after record rainfall soaked Allegheny County, meteorologists warn that a building heat dome will push Pittsburgh-area highs near 90 degrees this week, part of a dangerous stretch of heat blanketing much of the country.

sources.title: Dangerous heat wave is building, will bring oppressive temperatures to much of the United States
Western PA: Warming to 90 again this week

around_town.title: Washington Friendly-Fire Battlefield Grows Near Ligonier
around_town.latest_developments: The protected footprint of the 1758 friendly-fire battlefield tied to George Washington near Ligonier has expanded as researchers work to confirm a mass burial of soldiers on the site.
around_town.summary: In Westmoreland County near Ligonier, the ground where George Washington's Virginia troops mistakenly fired on fellow British soldiers in 1758 has grown as a preserved site, and researchers are trying to verify that a mass grave of the fallen lies within it.

sources.title: George Washington's friendly fire battlefield grows while researchers try to confirm mass burial of soldiers

around_teams.title: Brewers Scratch Misiorowski From Skenes Duel
around_teams.latest_developments: Milwaukee scratched hard-throwing rookie Jacob Misiorowski from his Sunday, July 12, start against Pirates ace Paul Skenes at PNC Park, scuttling the anticipated pitching matchup.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette reported the Milwaukee Brewers pulled young flamethrower Jacob Misiorowski from his scheduled Sunday start at PNC Park, undoing the marquee duel with Pittsburgh's Paul Skenes that had drawn attention to the series finale.

sources.title: Brewers star Jacob Misiorowski scratched from Sunday Skenes showdown

around_teams.title: Inside the Pirates' Konnor Griffin Draft Gambit
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette detailed how general manager Ben Cherington's front office maneuvered around the Chicago White Sox and Washington Nationals to land shortstop Konnor Griffin in the MLB Draft.
around_teams.summary: In a beat deep-dive, the Post-Gazette recounted the behind-the-scenes machinations by Ben Cherington and the Pittsburgh Pirates that secured shortstop prospect Konnor Griffin, tracing how the picks around them fell.

sources.title: The inside story of how the Pirates landed Konnor Griffin in the MLB Draft

team_usa.title: America Embraces Its Home World Cup
team_usa.latest_developments: With the United States men's team eliminated, the Guardian chronicled how packed stadiums and record television audiences have turned the co-hosted World Cup into a national phenomenon.
team_usa.summary: The Guardian reported that the 2026 World Cup, co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, has filled stadiums and set American viewership records, becoming a unifying cultural moment even after the United States men's team exited in the round of 16 to Belgium.

sources.title: 'A brilliant reprieve, a unifying force': America falls in love with World Cup
